THIS WEEK IN LOCAL GOVERNMENT

Wausau's Finance Committee advanced key decisions on lead pipe replacement and a downtown apartment project, while Weston trustees approved a new Bicycle and Pedestrian Plan and took stock of a tight 2027 budget.

  • The Wausau Finance Committee voted to fully fund lead service line replacements for the rest of the program, with bids targeting a December–January release for the 2027 season.
  • Weston's Board of Trustees approved the village's Bicycle and Pedestrian Plan 6-1, sending it to Marathon County upon formal adoption, and approved a Camp Phillips condominium plat by the same margin.
  • The Wausau Finance Committee approved a 2-1 budget modification clearing the way for a developer payment tied to the 700 Grand Avenue apartment project, with payment due within 30 days of verified completion.
  • Weston trustees and the Finance and HR Committee held a joint budget workshop on the 2027 budget but deferred final decisions on wages, pay structure, and borrowing to their October 5 meeting.
  • The Kronenwetter Plan Commission approved a conditional use permit for a Marathon County Highway Department garage and a lot-line adjustment on Wood Road/Tracy Court; the Green Tree subdivision plat moves to the Village Board.
  • The Kronenwetter Village Board is set to consider the Green Tree Trails Subdivision preliminary plat, a zero lot line text amendment, and a preview of the 2027 budget at its Monday meeting.

Coming up: Monday is a busy night across the region: the Wausau School Board holds its Annual Meeting Budget Hearing and multiple related sessions at 5 p.m., while the Kronenwetter Village Board meets at 6 p.m. to act on the Green Tree subdivision plat and budget preview. Weston's Comprehensive Plan Steering Committee and Parks & Recreation Committee also convene Monday, with the Weston Board of Trustees meeting again Tuesday, September 29.
